description: How far a source column's NOT NULL travels into a view's reported columns - the rule is SYNTACTIC: a projected column reference carries it (through aliases, qualification, SELECT *, WHERE/GROUP BY/ORDER BY/DISTINCT/LIMIT, derived tables, CTEs and views over views) and nothing else does - not a cast, COALESCE, COUNT(*), MAX or a literal; an outer join clears the null-extended side and any set operation clears it even when every branch is NOT NULL; SHOW COLUMNS agrees in both its data_type descriptor and its own null? spelling. All live-measured. The known parenthesized-reference divergence (live carries NOT NULL through SELECT (v), Frostlake does not) is deliberately unasserted, as in the Java. Converted 1:1 from ddl/ViewColumnNullabilityTest (now retired).
